issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual specification) defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (it states the method should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise). The solution repository instead declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() returning a String and implements Goat/Seal to return human-readable Strings. This mismatch between the specified return type (boolean) and the solution implementation (String) is structural and will confuse students about the correct interface contract and expected implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement to specify that messageOnMilk() returns a String (and document the expected message format), or (B) change the solution to match the current specification: declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return boolean and update Goat and Seal to return boolean (e.g. true when milking succeeds). If choosing (B), also update places that print messageOnMilk() (e.g., Main.java) to print a descriptive message instead of the boolean, or provide an additional String-returning method for human-readable milking messages.
